_doc: Fixed sprite camera (06_STYLE_ART.md section 3, 07 section 2.4). Orthographic, one pitch for every facing. The camera never moves between facings; the character turns on the spot. Director's pick 2026-10-08/09 (from docs/audits/realistic_density/): realistic proportions, density B = 84 px in a 55-degree world, sprites rendered at 45 degrees (D). Scale authority: px_per_m_1x, pinned to the 55-degree world so one sprite texel is one logical pixel in the stage: px_per_m_1x = world_char_height_px / (reference_height_m * cos(world_pitch_deg)). char_height_px is derived (px_per_m_1x * reference_height_m * cos(pitch_deg)): the figure stands taller in pixels at the shallower sprite pitch, which is correct. The render is render_scale times larger, and pixelate.py reduces it by exactly render_scale.
pitch_doc: sprite camera, degrees below horizontal (director D, 2026-10-09); shallower than the world so a realistic head reads above the shoulders
world_doc: the game camera's pitch (director, 2026-10-08); the sprite scale is pinned to it
world_char_height_doc: density B (director, 2026-10-09): a standing average_m is 84 logical px at the 55-degree world scale (960 x 540 logical, x2 at 1080p, x4 at 4K)
char_height_doc: derived, not chosen: px_per_m_1x * 1.78 * cos(45) = 84 * cos45 / cos55
reference_doc: average_m standing height (bodies/bodies.json); giant and slight bodies use the same px_per_m so a giant is taller on screen
frame_doc: square cell at 1x. Measured on realistic average_m (rest stance) at 45 degrees and this scale: the figure reaches 109 px above the pivot, 10 below and 21 either side; 176 leaves headroom for helmets and raised weapons.
pivot_doc: feet centre (world origin) in 1x cell pixels, x from the left, y from the top; the camera is aimed so the origin lands on this pixel. 24 px are left below the pivot; toes nearer the camera project up to 10 px below it at 45 degrees.
feet_tolerance_doc: validate_sheet.py: a frame's lowest opaque row may sit this far above the pivot or below it (toes toward the camera; measured 2..10 below at 45 degrees, plus 2). Pitch-dependent, so it lives with the pitch.
distance_doc: orthographic, so distance only has to clear the body; it does not change scale

facings.order_doc: facing k turns the character k * step_deg counter-clockwise seen from above. S (k=0) faces the camera; SE (k=1) faces the camera turned towards screen right; N (k=4) shows the back. Names are screen directions with S = towards the viewer.
